key_insight: A Mamba-based generative language model combined with data augmentation and an experience-replay memory yields sample-efficient generation of property-optimized small molecules, cutting the need for large labeled datasets or many expensive evaluations.
problem_solved: Reduces the data and evaluation burden in molecular generative design by improving sample efficiency and steering generation toward molecules with desired properties despite limited training examples.
method: Fine-tune a Mamba-based language model to generate SMILES/chemical strings for small molecules.
Apply targeted data augmentation to expand the effective training set and diversify candidate molecules.
Use experience replay / a memory buffer to store high-quality candidates and bias subsequent generation toward property-optimized molecules (memory manipulation).
impact: Enables faster, cheaper iterative design cycles in drug discovery and materials screening by lowering dependency on large datasets and costly property evaluations; practical for ML teams building generative chemistry pipelines.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart: pretraining → data augmentation → model generation → memory buffer (experience replay) → property evaluation → loop back

paper_title: Sample-efficient generative molecular design using memory manipulation
paper_authors: Jeff Guo, Junwu Chen, Anthony GX-Chen, Philippe Schwaller
